name: Liftwright
positioning: Liftwright is the no-nonsense strength gym for people who want real barbell coaching, honest programming and a floor built for lifting heavy.
audience: Beginner-to-intermediate lifters aged 20-45 who are tired of glossy fitness clubs and want structured strength training, platforms and racks, and coaches who actually teach technique.
strategy: Own the loud, raw end of the gym market with poster-like creative that feels like a flyer on a warehouse door. Lead with structure (programs, blocks, coached sessions) rather than body-image promises, and build community through recurring free events like the Saturday Deadlift Social.

contrastPairs.use: body and display text on red blocks
large display type only (never body text)

fonts.mono: None (Barlow 800 uppercase, wide tracking, for labels and data)

designSystem.spacing: 8px base unit; blocks use 64-128px vertical padding; full-bleed sections with 16-64px gutters
designSystem.radius: 0 everywhere. Hard corners only; the only curves are barbell plates
designSystem.borders: 3px solid Chalk or Lime rules; hazard-tape bands as section dividers
designSystem.imagery: No photos. Original vector barbells, plates and racks, halftone dot fields and hazard stripes
designSystem.shapes: Parallelograms skewed -12deg, diagonal slashes, stacked full-bleed bands
designSystem.buttons: Skewed parallelogram, Lime fill, black Anton uppercase label; hover shifts to Hazard Red
designSystem.cards: Flat black or chalk blocks with a 3px rule, oversized outline numerals, no shadows
designSystem.motifs: Massive condensed uppercase type, diagonal slashes, halftone textures, hazard-tape stripes

artDirection: Every piece should read like a gym-door poster from across the room: one massive Anton headline, often breaking the grid or bleeding off the edge, set in Chalk or Volt Lime on Floor Black. Add one diagonal Hazard Red slash and one halftone dot field per composition, and use hazard tape to separate information. Supporting copy is short, direct Barlow; CTAs are skewed lime parallelograms. Never show bodies or before/after imagery; show equipment, numbers and structure instead.
